title: Minimum Steps to Convert String with Operations
summary: Given two equal-length strings, word1 and word2, determine the least number of operations needed to convert word1 into word2.
statement: Given two equal-length strings, word1 and word2, determine the least number of operations needed to convert word1 into word2. Operations include replacing a character, swapping two characters, or reversing a substring. Each character in a substring can be used in at most one operation of each type.
constraints: The lowercase strings have equal length at most 100.
Partition word1 into substrings; within each, replacements, disjoint swaps, and at most one whole-substring reversal each cost one.
Minimize the total operations needed to produce word2.
hints: After an optional reversal, one swap fixes two mismatches exactly when their source-target pairs are inverses; all others need replacement.
Compute each interval cost in normal and reversed orientation, then use prefix DP over every final substring boundary.
Count directed mismatch pairs, cancel inverse pairs as swaps, compare normal cost with one plus reversed cost, and relax dp[end].
Every chosen partition is represented by its last boundary; within an interval, inverse pairing maximizes two-for-one corrections and remaining mismatches independently require replacements.
editorial: Every chosen partition is represented by its last boundary; within an interval, inverse pairing maximizes two-for-one corrections and remaining mismatches independently require replacements.

tests.explanation: Partitioning into ab, c, and df permits one reversal, one swap-equivalent correction, and replacements for a total of four.
Reverse the whole source and then use one swap to reach the target in two operations.
